title: How Red Richards's Saints and Sinners started, and earlier trumpeters
summary: A booker named Lou Pozey founded the group in Ohio with Vic Dickenson; earlier trumpeters included Wild Bill Davison and perhaps Dick Carey, and Autrey knew Eddie Condon's circle.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well let's get to -- how did you start working with Red? You were working with him, you said, with Frank Carey.
Yeah, that was one night here, doing other different -- one night, you know, what we call club dates.
How did the Saints and Sinners get started?

Well he had the Saints and Sinners. He was -- they were working out in Ohio, Columbus, Ohio, by the way. Lou [Pozey], I don't know if you've heard of him. He was -- he founded the -- Red and his group, and got them together, gave them and the name. He was booking them.
Who? Oh, he was a booker? Lou [Pozey]?
Yeah, uh-huh. And he was very much liked by the people who knew him, and -- well I met him slightly on the very end, and he passed later.
Oh, I see.

And they worked Columbus, Ohio, Cleveland, Detroit, and I'm trying -- I think yes, they worked Chicago. And they had a good band. Vic Dickenson, and Red, and _____ was on drum. They -- I wasn't there then.
Who was on trumpet before you were there?
Hm, hm-hm-hm, white fellow (Snaps fingers.)
Wild Bill was in the group for a --
Wild Bill, yeah.
Was that before, or after, you?

No, that's before, because -- but Wild -- he worked with Wild Bill -- Red Richards worked with Wild Bill's band a hell of a long time. Yeah. And Muggsy. Yeah. He worked with that band for a heck of a long time. And also -- I'm trying to think, who was this guy? He went to California, and I never did -- I heard of him. I never met him. And --
This is the white trumpet player?
Yeah. Joe Barifaldi was playing tenor with him. Because I met Joe, and Joe's a very good man, tenor
2nd clarinet.
Was the trumpet player Dick Carey?
I know Dick. I think Dick might have worked with them on a few things, maybe. I know -- I knew Dick very well. Dick played piano and trumpet.
Yeah, I know.
Yeah, uh-huh.
And played peckhorn, too, didn't he?
Yeah.
Everything.
And I tell you, he and I worked together with Eddie -- Eddie Condon.--
Eddie Condon.
-- on quite a few things. And I'm fun with fond of Eddie. I worked with him for years, in and out there.
Well then when you joined the Saints and Sinners it had been going for quite a while.

Yeah, they had been going, and they'd been to the coast, and back, because I heard Red talking -- had Red Vic Dick talking about it, you know. And oh, they were in -- he -- well he sounded -- he asked me to come with them about a year -- almost a year, maybe it was a year, doggone close, asked me to go with them, and I couldn't make it, because I had pneumonia. See what I mean?
